modules.title: 一次保存怎样经过等待、成功和错误状态

items.title: 记录当前而非永远
items.text: 用户点击保存后，页面记住“正在提交”，以避免重复点击并显示等待；请求结束后再改为成功或错误。

items.title: 状态驱动画面
items.text: 同一按钮和提示区会根据当前值显示不同内容。状态变化应来自真实操作或请求结果，不能只靠把成功文案提前写上去。

items.title: 代码里的状态长什么样
items.text: 在 React 里，最常见的就是 useState。比如 useState(false) 就创建了一个初始值为 false 的状态。当用户点击时，代码调用 setter 函数改变它的值，React 就会自动更新界面。所以当 AI 说“加个 loading 状态”时，通常就是指建一个控制 spinner 显隐的布尔值变量。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 状态不是组件，也不自动等于数据库。组件是界面责任的边界；数据库保存跨设备、跨用户需要长期保留的数据。页面刷新后丢失的临时状态，不能证明服务端已经保存成功。

lessonPractice.title: 用户点击保存后，页面立刻显示“已保存”，但请求随后失败。应该怎样修改？

options.label: 先显示“保存中”，成功后显示“已保存”，失败时提供重试
options.feedback: 对。等待、成功和失败是不同状态，页面要根据真实请求结果切换。

options.label: 先乐观显示“已保存”，失败时只记到控制台，不回滚界面
options.feedback: 这会把界面文案当成证据，用户会以为数据已经成功保存。

options.label: 提交期间禁用按钮，结束后无论成功失败都恢复成初始状态
options.feedback: 禁用按钮只能防止重复提交，不能告诉用户结果。成功和失败必须进入不同的可见状态。

en.title: A page shows “Saved” immediately after a click, but the network request then fails. What change fits best?

options.label: Enter a Saving state first, show Saved only after success, and show a retryable error on failure
options.feedback: Correct. Pending, success, and failure are different states, and the interface should change from the actual request result.

options.label: Keep showing Saved immediately because users dislike waiting
options.feedback: That treats interface text as proof and makes users think data was stored when it was not.

options.label: Remove every status message so no error text appears
options.feedback: People still need to know whether an action is pending, succeeded, or failed. Removing feedback does not make state accurate.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查这个保存流程的状态：点击后按钮显示“保存中”并禁用重复提交；只有接口成功才显示“已保存”，失败时显示错误和重试入口。改完后分别验证成功和失败两种结果。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Check the state in this save flow: after a click, show Saving and prevent duplicate submission; show Saved only after the API succeeds; show an error and retry path on failure. Verify both success and failure afterward.

learning.assumes: You have used a modal that opens and closes or seen a button change from Submit to Saving.
learning.outcome: You can identify which state changes across an action and ask for accurate pending, success, and error feedback.

modules.title: How one save moves through pending, success, and error

items.title: Remember the current condition
items.text: After Save is clicked, the page records that it is submitting, preventing repeat clicks and showing progress; it then changes to success or error when the request ends.

items.title: State drives what appears
items.text: The same button and message area show different content for different values. A state change should come from an actual action or request result, not an early success label.

items.title: What state looks like in code
items.text: In React, useState is the most common way to declare state. For example, useState(false) creates a state that starts as false. When the user clicks, the code calls the setter function to change the value, and React automatically updates the UI to match. When AI says “add a loading state”, it usually means creating a boolean state variable to toggle a spinner.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: State is neither a component nor automatically a database. A component marks an interface responsibility; a database holds information that must persist across devices or users. Temporary page state disappearing on refresh cannot prove a server saved anything.

distinctions.label: Component
distinctions.text: {c:state} records a current value or phase. A {c:component} reads that state and renders the matching interface.
